newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa April new car sales up 0.3 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa April new car sales up 0.3 percent yr/yr.

text.p: New car sales rose 0.3 percent year-on-year in April to 19,206 units but fell 9.0 percent from March's 21,110 units, the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa said on Tuesday.

The association said in a statement new car sector's growth momentum had slowed fairly sharply compared to previous months which could in part be attributed to the effects of recent sporadic industrial disruption at certain plants.
In aggregate terms, new vehicle sales for the first four months of the year remained ahead of the corresponding period in 1996, but only by a marginal 1.3 percent.

The combination of high levels of indebtedness, continued high real domestic interest rates and the effects of the recent round of new vehicle price increases would serve to reinforce expected consolidation in new vehicle market segments during the months ahead, Naamsa said.
In contrast, new vehicle exports had continued their strong trend in the first three months of the year, jumping 157.7 percent compared with the same period in 1996.

Toyota 8,060, Samcor 4,846, Delta 4,499, Volkswagen 4,198, Nissan 2,958, Mercedes-Benz 2,851, BMW 1,029, Daewoo 615, Land Rover SA 259, Chrysler 133, MAN 32, Tyco 50, Iveco 120, AAD 22, Freightliner 33, ERF 13, Subaru 12, Scania 19.
